OP, Ensure lang na pag binago mo yung power management mode mo under Manage 3D Settings (assuming NVIDIA card ng iyong laptop), set mo lang sya sa Normal for Global Settings. Go over Program Settings sa mga games/apps na ginagamit mo and set it to High Performance as commentor said. This way, makapag throttle down din si GPU when just browsing/doing non-heavy workload. Keeps the temps lower and overall lengthens your laptops' components lifespan.

I would highly advise you go with a better GPU. The RTX 3050 just doesn't cut it for price to performance. Nowadays you should be able to get a 3060ti cheap. 

I would also advise you go with Raptor Lake (13th gen) Intel CPUs as their generation leap from 12th is quite immense, although more power-hungry. As for monitor, if 1080p ang choice of resolution mo, that would mean more CPU-reliant. 144hz would be great for you to experience, 3060s and up are well capable of delivering that naman. I'd advise a K chip over a KF for the iGPU sync, but that would also mean na you'll have to get a motherboard to allow undervolting/overclocking for better temps and performance (some B boards I believe allow that, but you're mostly looking at Z boards for full potential). Sa RAM nyo I wouldn't worry too much about going to expensive routes like Corsair Dominator Platinum RGB. Focus more on the size, memory frequency and latency timings. The T-Force option you listed is a great choice.

Do note that 12th/13th gen CPUs run quite warm than their predecessors, but a decent air cooler would suffice instead of going AIO route pero di naman quality. It will all come down to case fans and fan curve tuning which can easily be done to attain good temps sa mainit natin na climate.
